notes:
Summary: enterprise retail company evaluating Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing chat + catalog reranking. High ops sensitivity - must support on-prem options for EU compliance and prefer VPC for US traffic. Workshop held 2026-02-17 with AE + SE + infra team. Key quant findings from synthetic load and baseline telemetry:

- Current prod baseline (observed): ~25 QPS steady-state for chat endpoint; avg payload ~300 tokens/request (~7.5k tokens/sec steady).
- Peak behavior: marketing events create short spikes up to ~250 QPS (observed 10x bursts), average tokens during spikes ~300 => ~75k tokens/sec peak.
- Embeddings/semantic search traffic runs separately: steady 5 QPS with large embedding jobs (avg 1024 tokens) during nightly windows; concurrent with daytime peaks increases GPU needs.

Workshop capacity takeaways / recommendations:
- Measured throughput per GPU (Redwood test harness, optimized runtime):
  - H100 (private pool, quant-friendly): ~30 QPS for 300-token chat with p95 ~120-180ms (no heavy sampling).
  - A100 80GB equivalent: ~22 QPS for same workload, p95 ~180-220ms.
- Sizing math (conservative): target baseline 25 QPS => 1 H100 covers baseline headroom for chat. Peak 250 QPS => ~9 H100s raw; recommend reserved pool 11 H100s for 20% headroom + capacity for embeddings batch windows. If using A100s, recommend 15 reserved.
- Tokens/sec view: steady ~7.5k toks/s, peak ~75k toks/s. Plan caching and prefix KV for common flows to reduce effective tokens/sec by 15-30% for chat reuse patterns.
- Batching/autoscale: combine reserved pool (capacity guarantee) + burst autoscaling credits for unpredictable spikes. Proposed policy: reserved capacity handles 80% steady/peak baseline; burst credits cover remaining 20% to avoid immediate procurement of extra GPUs.

SLO & SLA negotiation notes:
- Requested latency targets: p95 <= 200ms for short prompts (<512 tokens), p95 <= 600ms for long prompts. Redwood proposed default p95 250ms and offered tuning knobs (batching thresholds, smaller quantized model variant for low-latency tier).
- Uptime target: 99.95% desired; queue credits and SLA credit schedule discussed. Sable wants 72h advance notice for maintenance impacting reserved pool.
- Data plane: must support EU residency for PII. KMS integration required (bring-your-own-key ok). Logs + audit trail retention 2y requested.

Action items & next steps (short):
- Redwood: run 2nd workshop (deep bench) with Sable infra to validate H100 vs A100 per-customer model variants (scheduled 2026-03-05). Deliver written capacity plan and pricing by 2026-03-10. (AE Jordan)
